title: Privacy of Groups in Dense Street Imagery
source: Franchi, Sandhaus, Choksi, Engelmann, Ju & Nissenbaum · ACM FAccT 2025
blurb: When the sidewalk is photographed at scale, it isn't only individuals who are captured but whole groups. Group privacy is exactly what conventional, person-by-person protections miss.
authors: Franchi, Sandhaus, Choksi, Engelmann, Ju & Nissenbaum

title: Detecting disparities in police deployments using dashcam data
source: Franchi, Zamfirescu-Pereira, Ju & Pierson · ACM FAccT 2023
blurb: A fleet of rideshare dashcams becomes a city-scale sensing network, here used to measure where police are deployed across New York and surface the disparities in who gets watched.

title: Nexar dashcam video database hacked
blurb: A breach exposed 130+ TB of dashcam footage from Nexar's cloud. The dashcam layer in this map is a real, breachable archive of faces and places.

title: Bill requiring smart glasses to show a recording indicator
source: Rep. Joe Ciresi (H.B. 2603) · PA House · June 2026
blurb: Pennsylvania moves to mandate a visible light whenever smart glasses record. A direct policy response to the covert-capture problem the "In 5 years…" glasses layer imagines.

title: Meta's Ray-Ban glasses users film and harass massage-parlor workers
blurb: Instagram accounts with huge followings repost covert Ray-Ban-glasses footage of people at massage parlors. The smart-glasses layer's harm is already here, not five years out.

title: ICE Taps into Nationwide AI-Enabled Camera Network
source: Jason Koebler & Joseph Cox · 404 Media · May 2025
blurb: Local police quietly run Flock license-plate searches for ICE — 4,000+ lookups with no federal contract. The red plate-reader layer here is a slice of that same network, now national infrastructure.

title: The Follower
blurb: A surveillance artist matched influencers' Instagram posts to weeks of footage from the same public cameras. This map's premise made personal: the open camera already holds a version of you.

title: Waymo's Driverless Cars Revealed to Be Narcs as Cops Use Them to Probe Crimes
blurb: Police now pull 360° footage from robotaxis to work cases. Every driverless car is a roving camera — the moving-sensor logic of the dashcam and bus layers here, minus the driver.

title: Inside the NYPD's Surveillance Machine
blurb: Thousands of volunteers mapped 15,000+ NYPD-reachable cameras wired for facial recognition. It's the crowdsourced census the fixed-CCTV layer in this map is built on.
